title: Implement Rand10() Using Rand7()
notes:
Task: Generate a uniform integer from 1 through 10 using only rand7().
Idea: Combine two rand7() calls into a uniform value from 1 through 49; reject values above 40 and map accepted values to 1..10.
Invariant: Every integer 1..49 is equally likely before rejection, so each accepted output has the same number of preimages.
Edge cases: Rejection is necessary to avoid modulo bias; rand7() is provided by the judge.
complexity_reason: Each attempt uses two random calls and succeeds with probability 40/49.

title: Implement Rand10() Using Rand7()
notes:
Task: Produce an unbiased uniform integer in [1,10] using the provided rand7().
Idea: Generate a uniform integer from 1 through 49, reject the last nine outcomes, and map the remaining 40 outcomes evenly to 1..10.
Invariant: Each accepted output corresponds to exactly four equally likely input outcomes.
Edge cases: The method loops until an acceptable value appears; rand7() is judge-provided.
complexity_reason: Each attempt succeeds with probability 40/49 and uses constant work.

title: Matchsticks to Square
notes:
Task: Use every matchstick to form four equal-length sides.
Idea: Reject totals not divisible by four, sort sticks descending, and backtrack while assigning each stick to a side without exceeding target.
Invariant: At each recursion level, the side sums contain exactly the already assigned sticks.
Edge cases: The largest stick cannot exceed target; symmetric empty-side choices are skipped to reduce duplicate search.
complexity_reason: Each stick may be tried on up to four sides and recursion depth is n.

title: Matchsticks to Square
notes:
Task: Determine whether all matchsticks can form a square without cutting any stick.
Idea: Sort descending and recursively assign each stick to one of four side sums, pruning sums above target and symmetric side states.
Invariant: The four side totals reflect exactly the sticks assigned before the current recursion depth.
Edge cases: A non-divisible total or stick larger than target returns false immediately.
complexity_reason: The search may try four side assignments per stick and recurses once per stick.

title: Ones and Zeroes
notes:
Task: Maximize the number of selected binary strings using at most m zeros and n ones.
Idea: Count each string's zeros and ones, then update a 2D knapsack table in descending resource order.
Invariant: dp[i][j] is the largest subset size achievable with at most i zeros and j ones from processed strings.
Edge cases: Descending loops ensure each string is used at most once; strings containing only zeros or only ones are supported.
complexity_reason: Each string updates every feasible resource state; L is the number of strings.

title: Ones and Zeroes
notes:
Task: Choose the largest subset of binary strings within zero and one budgets m and n.
Idea: Use a 2D DP table and process each string as a 0/1 item with its zero and one counts as costs.
Invariant: dp[i][j] is the best subset size within i zeros and j ones after processed strings.
Edge cases: Iterate both budgets downward so a string cannot be selected more than once.
complexity_reason: Each string is processed across the 2D budget table.

title: Heaters
notes:
Task: Find the minimum common radius so every house is covered by a heater.
Idea: Sort heater positions and use binary search to find each house's nearest heater on either side.
Invariant: Each house's required radius is the smaller distance to its nearest left or right heater.
Edge cases: Houses are assumed nonempty and at least one heater exists; the maximum nearest distance is the required radius.
time_complexity: O(m log m + n log m)
complexity_reason: Sorting heaters and binary-searching once per house dominate the runtime.

title: Heaters
notes:
Task: Minimize the radius shared by all heaters so every house is covered.
Idea: Sort heater locations and binary-search the insertion point for each house.
Invariant: The nearest heater must be the closest heater on the left or right of the house.
Edge cases: A house before the first or after the last heater has only one candidate side.
time_complexity: O(m log m + n log m)
complexity_reason: The heaters are sorted and each house uses binary search for its nearest neighbors.

title: Number Complement
notes:
Task: Flip the significant binary bits of a positive integer and return the resulting value.
Idea: Create an all-ones mask with the same bit length and XOR it with num.
Invariant: The mask contains ones only at positions from the most significant set bit down to zero.
Edge cases: Positive input is guaranteed; zero is outside the original problem's constraints.
complexity_reason: Bit length and XOR require constant machine-word operations.

title: Number Complement
notes:
Task: Return the complement using only the number's significant bits.
Idea: Build a mask of ones through the highest set bit and XOR with num.
Invariant: The mask excludes all higher leading-zero positions from the complement.
Edge cases: The problem supplies a positive integer, so at least one significant bit exists.
complexity_reason: The mask is shifted once per bit in the positive input.

title: Total Hamming Distance
notes:
Task: Sum the Hamming distance over all unordered pairs of numbers.
Idea: At each bit position, count ones and zeros; every one pairs with every zero to contribute a differing bit.
Invariant: For a bit with c ones among n values, its contribution is c*(n-c).
Edge cases: Duplicate values contribute zero distance between themselves; fixed-width nonnegative integers fit within the scanned bit range.
complexity_reason: Each of 32 bit positions scans the array once.

title: Total Hamming Distance
notes:
Task: Compute the sum of pairwise Hamming distances for all array pairs.
Idea: Count set bits independently at each bit position and multiply ones by zeros.
Invariant: Every pair differing at a bit contributes exactly once to ones*(n-ones).
Edge cases: Use a long accumulator for the total; 32 bit positions cover the integer representation.
complexity_reason: The algorithm scans all values for each of 32 bit positions.

title: Generate Random Point in a Circle
notes:
Task: Generate a uniform random point inside a circle with the supplied radius and center.
Idea: Choose a uniform angle and radius R*sqrt(U), where U is uniform on [0,1), then convert polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates.
Invariant: The square-root radial transform makes probability proportional to area rather than radius.
Edge cases: Points may lie on the boundary only with negligible probability; the constructor parameters are stored by the object.
complexity_reason: A constant number of random and trigonometric operations generates each point.

title: Generate Random Point in a Circle
notes:
Task: Generate random points uniformly over the area of a circle.
Idea: Sample angle uniformly and radius as R*sqrt(U), then translate the polar point by the circle center.
Invariant: Squaring the sampled radius gives a uniform fraction of the circle's area.
Edge cases: The generated coordinates remain within radius R of the center; the random point is not expected to be reproducible.
complexity_reason: Each call performs a constant number of random and trigonometric operations.

title: License Key Formatting
notes:
Task: Reformat a license key into uppercase groups of k characters separated by dashes.
Idea: Remove existing dashes, uppercase the characters, and group from the right in chunks of size k.
Invariant: Every group except possibly the first has exactly k characters.
Edge cases: The first group may be shorter; an empty normalized key returns an empty string.
complexity_reason: The string is filtered and regrouped once; output storage is linear.

title: License Key Formatting
notes:
Task: Normalize a license key to uppercase and group characters from the right in blocks of size k.
Idea: Remove dashes, uppercase letters, then insert separators every k characters from the end.
Invariant: Each non-first group has exactly k characters.
Edge cases: A short first group is allowed and an empty key yields an empty string.
complexity_reason: Normalization and grouping scan the input once and build an output string.

title: Max Consecutive Ones
notes:
Task: Find the longest contiguous run of ones in a binary array.
Idea: Increment the current run for one and reset it at zero, tracking the maximum.
Invariant: curr is the length of the current suffix of consecutive ones.
Edge cases: Empty arrays return zero; a run ending at the final element is included in the maximum.
complexity_reason: One pass tracks only the current and maximum streaks.

title: Max Consecutive Ones
notes:
Task: Return the maximum number of consecutive ones in a binary array.
Idea: Track the current run and reset it to zero on every zero.
Invariant: best is the longest run seen so far, and curr is the run ending at the current position.
Edge cases: Empty arrays return zero and all-one arrays return their length.
complexity_reason: The array is scanned once with two counters.

title: Predict the Winner
notes:
Task: Decide whether the first player can secure a score at least as high as the second by taking either end each turn.
Idea: Let dp[i][j] be the best score difference the current player can force on interval i..j.
Invariant: Choosing the left or right value subtracts the opponent's best difference on the remaining interval.
Edge cases: A one-element array is won by player one; ties count as a win.
complexity_reason: The interval DP fills O(n^2) states in a rolling one-dimensional array.

title: Predict the Winner
notes:
Task: Determine whether player one can achieve a score at least equal to player two.
Idea: Use interval DP where each state is the maximum score difference obtainable by the player whose turn it is.
Invariant: dp[i] stores the best score difference for interval i..j as the interval length expands.
Edge cases: A tie is considered a win for player one; a single element gives a nonnegative difference.
complexity_reason: The nested interval loops process O(n^2) states using one DP array.
